name: Synhexyl
summary: Parahexyl, also known as synhexyl, is a synthetic homologue of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) which was invented in 1941 during attempts to elucidate the structure of Δ9-THC, one of the active components of cannabis.

pharmacology.text: Parahexyl produces effects typical of other cannabinoid receptor agonists in animals. Presumably, it acts as a CB1 receptor agonist in the same way as THC, but as there has been no research published using parahexyl since the discovery of the CB1 receptor, this has not been definitively confirmed.

uses.en: It was used in early cannabis research and briefly tested as a treatment for depression. Today it is mainly of historical interest.
uses.zh: 它曾用於早期的大麻研究，也短暫被試驗用於治療憂鬱症。如今它主要只具有歷史意義。
uses.zhHans: 它曾用于早期的大麻研究，也短暂被试验用于治疗忧郁症。如今它主要只具有历史意义。

sideEffects.en: Little modern research exists. As a THC-like cannabinoid, it would be expected to cause effects such as dry mouth, red eyes, a racing heart, anxiety and poor short-term memory.
sideEffects.zh: 現代相關研究很少。作為類似THC的大麻素，預期它會造成口乾、眼睛發紅、心跳加速、焦慮與短期記憶變差等影響。
sideEffects.zhHans: 现代相关研究很少。作为类似THC的大麻素，预期它会造成口干、眼睛发红、心跳加速、焦虑与短期记忆变差等影响。

fact.en: It was invented in 1941 by the chemist Roger Adams and his team while they were trying to work out the structure of THC. In the 1940s it was even tried as a treatment for depression.
fact.zh: 它在1941年由化學家羅傑．亞當斯的團隊在試圖解出THC結構時發明。1940年代時，它甚至被試用來治療憂鬱症。
fact.zhHans: 它在1941年由化学家罗杰．亚当斯的团队在试图解出THC结构时发明。1940年代时，它甚至被试用来治疗忧郁症。
